###Is signing up For a Dog Grooming Course Worth Your While?

If you are serious about becoming a dog groomer, you need to be able to inspire confidence and trust in your prospective clients. One of the easiest ways to do so is to sign up either for a physical dog grooming school, or to enroll for an online course in dog grooming. What is the difference and which is more worth your time and money?

###Online dog grooming schools:

These online courses are generally provided in a 12-week certification course, or a longer 24-week diploma program, and are one of the most popular ways to go about gaining a qualification as they can be accessed from home at any time, so are ideal for people already working and wanting to study towards becoming a dog groomer part time, while still supplementing their income.

However, dog grooming is a physical occupation, and there is only so much know-how that can be obtained through an online dog grooming program. So while these are a great way to build up your knowledge, become familiar with dog grooming terminology, and of course gain a qualification; it will still be essential to do some hands-on work with dogs as well. What an online course does offer is the opportunity to increase your knowledge of dog breeds and behaviour, skin conditions, products and styling terminology, and they are generally reasonably priced.

**Conventional hands-on dog training schools:**

Working with dogs under the supervision of a qualified and experienced dog groomer is the fastest and most thorough way to gain a dog grooming qualification – the drawbacks of course are that you are limited geographically to areas where the schools are available. You will also need to be able to commit large chunks of your time on a regular basis to attending lessons, and exercise discipline just as you would with a college or university course, and they can be relatively expensive compared with an online course.

The benefits of having a dedicated tutor, with all of their experience, advice and know-how at your disposal is invaluable, and you will also learn about physically handling large or nervous dogs, practise using the various grooming tools and get an idea of how you would value a quote for a prospective client.

**Alternatives:**

An alternative to attending an online or physical dog grooming school, is to work as a shadow employee or volunteer at an existing dog grooming salon or parlour. In place of a certificate or diploma, you may well receive a glowing recommendation from an existing and successful dog grooming service provider, which may be worth more in the eyes of a potential client than a piece of paper printed from the internet!

By working in this environment, you are not only exposed to the dogs and various groomers, along with their expertise, tips and tricks – but also to the business side of running a dog grooming business. You have access to all the behind the scenes daily dramas, financial administration, managing stock of the different products, dealing with customers, and all the ad-hoc responsibilities of a dog grooming service which you wouldn’t expect.

You may also have the option of joining a dog groomer who also operates a [mobile dog grooming](http://www.dogwiki.co/dog-grooming/mobile-dog-grooming/) service. If you can go along on their visits to clients you become exposed to yet another avenue of the dog grooming industry, which may in fact give you a potential starting point for your own business.

###Terminology – understanding the difference between dog grooming schools, programs, and courses:

Don’t let the different terminologies confuse you – ‘courses’ covers the basic skills of dog grooming such as brushing, combing, general grooming, cutting and clipping, keeping the work area sanitary and sterilized, as well as basic business operations and shop administration. A course will end in you being issued with a certificate.

A ‘program’ differs in that it offers a state-licensed diploma from either a recognised school or university, or other officially recognised academic institution. For example, the [National Dog Groomers Association of America ](https://www.nationaldoggroomers.com/)has various dog grooming school branches where they will conduct official tests in order to qualify to receive the diploma.

###What do you actually learn at a dog grooming school or working as a dog grooming volunteer?

Getting hands-on experience is your ultimate goal, whether you choose to pay to attend a dog grooming school, or work as a volunteer at an existing salon or dog grooming parlour. Some of the fields you will explore include:

* The ethics of dog grooming and ensuring the safety of the animal, as well as minimising stress * Brushing and combing techniques * Different clips and cuts, and grooming techniques * Dog anatomy * Caring for and sanitising dog grooming equipment * Selecting the right equipment for the job * Making sure the working area is sterile * And depending on where you reside, there may be official standards, such as the American Kennel Club, or the original Kennel Club in the UK, which have to be met.

If you are keen to start your own business, make sure that your grooming school also offers business classes, and ideally classes on treating ill or injured dogs, as your clients will be very likely to approach you as their first point of contact if they suspect something to be wrong with their dog. The more veterinary knowledge you can acquire, the better. It is also a good idea to make sure that you receive some first aid training for dog bites and scratches – just in case!

##Do I need my own equipment?

Many dog grooming schools will provide their own equipment for you to train with, and an existing practise will of course have their own equipment already. However, if you intend to start your own company, investing in your own [dog grooming equipment](http://www.dogwiki.co/shop/product-category/grooming/) that you can become familiar with using as soon as possible is an excellent idea. Some dog grooming schools will even require you to have your own equipment.

##What qualification will I receive?

This depends on whether the school is affiliated with a national organisation or qualifying authority, and also on the duration of the course. Some ‘schools’ may offer training, but are not authorised to issue diplomas. You will have to check this with the individual school you opt to attend to make sure you get the qualification level you are after.

##Tips on choosing a dog grooming school:

It is important to do a tour of the facilities of any school before you sign up with them – you don’t want to be associated with or support a facility which treats their animals unkindly. A trainer who is impatient or harsh with their animals is not going to make a great teacher either!

Are there sufficient trainers available to supervise not just the students, but the dogs as well? Look for small classes, where the trainer is able to give individual attention to students, as well as keeping an eye on the dogs – this means that accidents are far less likely, and will also ensure that you get the best one-on-one attention for your training.

Are the facilities kept clean and hygienic? Keeping up standards is very important for any dog grooming facility, and in a trade as messy as dog grooming, it is vital that conditions are kept as sanitary as possible at all times.

In essence, choose a dog grooming school that echoes the reason you decided to go into dog grooming in the first place – people who love dogs, and love seeing them pampered and taken care of. You will be rewarded with invaluable experience, and well set up on your way to becoming a world-class dog groomer!
